observable_features: Tall repeated window bays form a largely glazed upper facade between slender brick piers.
Glazing turns around the prominent corner instead of being enclosed by a massive solid corner block.
A long lower wing contrasts with the taller end volume, chimney and entrance block.
Straight roof edges, repeated bays and unadorned brick/glass surfaces organize the building's exterior.

association_evidence.supports: UNESCO identifies the Fagus Factory complex as designed around 1910 by Walter Gropius, relates its glass-panel functionalist industrial aesthetic to the development of modern architecture, and describes it as foreshadowing the Bauhaus school.

confusion_check.shared_appearances: Glazed bays and unornamented volumes also occur in Bauhaus and later architectural reduction.
confusion_check.discriminating_relationships: Retain as early functionalist architecture. State the historical/broader-narrower relationship rather than inventing a glass-facade test that makes Modernism and Bauhaus mutually exclusive.
confusion_check.cannot_conclude: The finding is limited to this recorded view/branch. Factory facade demonstrates one architectural branch, not all modernist practices.
